## Task statement

**Invariant.** Processing untrusted input is ~linear in time and capped in memory

**Oracle.** `size_sweep` growth exponent ≤ 1.4, `redos_probe` < 100 ms at 10k, peak RSS under cap

**Violation cases seeded.** quadratic regex; uncapped read; XML DTD; zip without budget

Source: `EVALS-PLAN.md` Layer 0.

## Construction

Every task is a directory `evals/cases/P2/<case>/` holding a `case.yaml` (the task record: `id`, `property`, `origin`, `grader`, `expect`, `description`, `canary`), a `vuln/` tree with exactly one planted violation, and a `clean/` twin — the same code with the violation fixed through the toolkit primitive. The grader scores both: the violation must be detected in `vuln/` (recall) and not in `clean/` (precision), so the clean twin is the baseline scored alongside every task.

Origins, in the priority order of EVALS-PLAN.md Layer 2:

- **historical-miss** (6): a real miss from this program, encoded permanently.
- **derived** (1): a violation case from the Layer 0 row, in a code shape the historical cases do not already cover.

| task | origin | grader | description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `P2-html-no-cap-01` | historical-miss | `refuse` | research-replication-agent intake.fetch_html_as_text: the page body was taken whole (response.text) and stripped to text under no byte ceiling, so a hostile "paper page" of any size was buffered and parsed. Clean reads the body through secprim.bounded_read under MAX_HTML_BYTES (the real fix moved the fetch to safe_fetch(max_bytes=...), which applies the same primitive). |
| `P2-html-strip-quadratic-01` | historical-miss | `cost` | research-replication-agent intake: the tag stripper re.sub(r"<[^>]+>", ...) re-scans to the end of the input from every unterminated "<", so a run of openers is O(n^2) (100k "<" = 2.7 s). Clean uses <[^<>]+>, which cannot straddle a tag, and removes script/style blocks with one forward scan instead of an opener-to-closer regex. |
| `P2-nested-quantifier-regex-01` | derived | `cost` | A header key list matched with ^(?:\w+\s?)+: — a quantified group whose body can also match the separator-less run, so letters with no terminating ":" are split every possible way. Nested quantifiers are exponential, not quadratic (24 letters = 0.8 s, 30 = a minute), so the probe runs at n=24; the clean rewrite with a mandatory separator, ^\w+(?:\s+\w+)*\s*:, is microseconds there and linear at any size. |
| `P2-read-before-size-check-01` | historical-miss | `refuse` | study-hub extract_text.xlsx_text: z.read("xl/sharedStrings.xml") ran before the size check, so a 200 KB workbook declaring a 200 MB part was decompressed in full (269 MB peak) and only then refused. Clean reads the member's declared size first and refuses with TooLarge before a byte is decompressed. The grader counts decompressed bytes, so "read everything, then raise" is also detected. |
| `P2-redact-header-regex-01` | historical-miss | `cost` | study-hub redact(): the first fix narrowed \s to [ \t] and was verified on newline runs only; [ \t]*-?[ \t]* was still ~O(n^2) on a run of spaces (10k spaces = 2.2 s). The eval probes every character class. |
| `P2-xml-dtd-01` | historical-miss | `refuse` | study-hub xlsx_text parsed sharedStrings.xml with xml.etree, which expands the entities an internal DTD declares (billion laughs). Clean parses through secprim.safe_xml_fromstring, which refuses any DOCTYPE/ENTITY declaration and caps the document size; a plain document still parses. |
| `P2-zip-no-budget-01` | historical-miss | `refuse` | smart-dispatch ingest_ercot_history: the annual archive's workbook was read with zf.read(zf.namelist()[0]) under no per-member, total or ratio budget, so a small archive declaring a huge member was decompressed in full. Clean admits members through secprim.safe_zip_members, which refuses on declared size before any byte is read. |

## Metrics and current numbers

- **recall** = tasks whose `vuln/` the grader detected ÷ tasks, Wilson 95% CI.
- **precision** = tasks whose `clean/` the grader did not flag ÷ tasks, Wilson 95% CI.
- with `--trials K > 1`: **pass@k** (any of k) and **pass^k** (all of k) over tasks.

## Known limitations

From the grader docstrings (what each oracle can and cannot decide):

### `cost`

> P2: bounded cost. Detected = super-linear / over-deadline behaviour.

### `refuse`

> Plugin grader `refuse` — the refusal oracle for P1 (boundary) and P2 (bounded
> cost). `fuzz` detects an *undeclared* exception and `cost` detects *time*; neither
> expresses "this input must be turned away": a `float()` that accepts "nan", a
> `root / relpath` that accepts "../x", a reader with no byte cap, an XML parser
> that accepts an entity declaration. Those all *return normally*. This grader
> feeds a fixed, hostile input set and requires a declared refusal for each.
>
>   refuse   expect: {target: "mod:fn",
>                     inputs: <named set> | [<value> | {kind: ..., ...}, ...],
>                     accept: <named set> | [...],        # optional: must NOT be refused
>                     refuse: [TooLarge],                 # exception names that count as a refusal
>                     max_read: N}                        # optional: bytes a target may consume first
>
> Named sets (literal values):
>   nonfinite    nan / inf in every spelling a query parameter can carry
>   finite_ok    ordinary numbers and numeric strings
>   path_escape  absolute, `..`, drive, UNC, NUL, empty — what contained_path refuses
>   path_ok      ordinary relative paths that stay inside the root
>
> Constructed inputs ({kind: ..., size: N, ...}):
>   zip_member   the PATH of a zip archive whose one member (`member`, default
>                "data.bin") declares `size` bytes of `fill` (compressible, the
>                default, or random); decompressed bytes are counted
>   response     a fake HTTP response of `size` bytes with .read/.iter_bytes/
>                .iter_content/.content/.text; bytes handed out are counted
>   xml_dtd      bytes of an XML document carrying an internal entity declaration
>
> A variant is DETECTED when any hostile input is not refused — the target returns,
> raises something outside `refuse`, or (counted kinds) consumes more than
> `max_read` bytes before refusing. An `accept` input that *is* refused is an
> error, not a pass: a twin that refuses everything proves nothing.
>
> Deterministic and offline: inputs are built in memory or in a temp dir, nothing
> depends on the clock, and the stdlib `zipfile` patch used for counting is
> restored in a `finally`.

## Contamination policy

- **Canary.** Every `case.yaml`, every registry entry and `tasks.jsonl` carry the string in `evals/registry/CANARY.txt` (BIG-bench convention): a model that can reproduce it has seen this corpus in training, and its scores on it do not measure the property.
- **Split.** This eval is `split: build`. Build-split cases are used to tune rules and defenses. The held-out split (`evals/heldout/`, EVALS-PLAN.md Phase 4) is sealed: written after the defenses, never used for tuning, and scored only in reports.
- **No model in the loop.** Every grader is deterministic code; no LLM judges a result, so there is nothing to contaminate on the grading side.
